Regarding the legal matter in Carter vs. Pearson, the evidence presented is highly relevant and credible for assessing the defense's claim of duress. The phone records showing repeated calls from unknown sources to Pearson's number around the time of the confession provide objective, contemporaneous data that supports the allegation of harassment or threats. This type of digital evidence is generally considered reliable in court to establish a timeline and corroborate witness testimony regarding the circumstances under which the confession was obtained. The relevance lies in its direct connection to the claim that Pearson was coerced, potentially rendering the written confession involuntary and inadmissible.
